rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Social media, attention, and trades", "body": "The conversation opened with Chance describing how a screen heavy job left him wanting to ground out in the sun, and he argued that the return of trades would make people happier and healthier. He said the hands on craft retained the attention and intention put into it. Chance described mainstream social platforms as resource extraction systems built to breed conflict and sell attention, and he said that was why he preferred Telegram, which he compared to the old internet. Both sides agreed the culture was sorting out which old ways to keep and which new ones to adopt."}, {"title": "Cycles and the year of our Lord", "body": "Asked when the world seemed to change, Chance said it was always changing, and he described a spiral of time in which cycles nearly but never exactly repeat. He gave his view that the phrase year of our Lord encoded the sky clock, noting that god names such as Janus and the name Anna contain the Latin word for year. Chance described the sky as the outer boundary of perception and compared what was visible in the sky to what was conscious. He said knowing the allegory of the heavens might amount to knowing the pattern of the mind of God."}, {"title": "Questioning the Gnostic prison story", "body": "Chance said he could not embrace the version of Gnosticism popular in truth circles, in which matter is a prison made by a lesser god. He explained that he would feel victimized by that belief, and he posed what he called the ultimate checkmate: why the real god would not simply fix the problem. Chance allowed that negative intention and energy harvesting exist but said they are not the point of this place. He added that people build systems reflecting their deepest beliefs, and he called the loosh farm idea an excuse for being out of control."}, {"title": "Waking others and mirrors of progress", "body": "Asked about waking up the sheeple, Chance answered that the premise carries a flaw, since asserting that people are asleep bakes in the condition one hopes to change, like a broken chain of logic in code. He suggested doing what feels like a full body yes and letting others come to you. Chance described family and old friends as a heads up display of one's own progress and as the slowest to change. A host shared a dream in which people were planets, and Chance said the unhealed parts of a person show up in their relationships."}, {"title": "Life as a game with a body manual", "body": "Chance said simulation in the old sense means hypocrisy, which he tied to the popularity of simulation theory among materialists. He preferred the metaphor of life as a game, because it took the edge off and allowed for enjoyment and growth. He repeated that, in his view, the body is in the mind and a microcosm of the whole, and he compared the spirit and body to a seed and a tree. Chance proposed a clickable biofield teaching tool and said it could serve as a user manual for the human game, and a host said they were excited to build it."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I recently had a fun hang with Reality Designers, riffing on topics such as staying tuned and awake in a world that's going crazier by the day, how what we see on the external is a reflection of our Internal State, and even some bits about modern gnosticism and the flaws and debunks in the code of these ideas we have collectively recognized and why we see reality differently. We also talked about Reality being a type of Video Game, and what that means for our souls evolution and whether to take life too seriously or not, if it were just a game after all.
